attacks.claimAttacked: pendingTerminalizerRecord preserves the permission carrier's single durable order while the journal is capacity-paused.
attacks.method: Persist a pending projectPurge outside an intact-tail journal at sequence n, crash, and ask which durable byte forbids an ordinary n+1 append before the terminal marker exists.
evidence: The external pending record, not any journal record, supplies the gate that makes the terminal marker the only lawful next append.

It also names the FIRST terminalizer by arrival. permission-truth-tables.v6 declares one durable append-only grant journal, no second ordering authority anywhere, and journal durability/sequence rather than arrival as its order.

SUP-124-GRANT-JOURNAL displaces class-containment and boundedness rules only; it does not name or authorize a second ordering authority. Using the same writer removes a two-writer race but does not collapse two durable orders into one.

attacks.claimAttacked: The pending-record write-failure clause remains fail-closed across crash and capacity recovery.
attacks.method: Reach capacityPause with a proven intact tail, deliver projectPurge, fail the required external pending write, crash, restore capacity, and recover using only declared durable bytes.
evidence: The writeRule says failure keeps the pause and MUST NOT resume, but the failed write leaves no pending record and capacityPause itself has no durable byte placement.
After crash the original arrival is unavailable. The capacityPause rule explicitly says that when capacity returns and the record is absent, ordinary appends resume.
No acceptance/refusal acknowledgement rule reclassifies the first terminalizer as never accepted, so the subject's FIRST-wins claim is lost as written.

blockers.title: pendingTerminalizerRecord is a second durable ordering authority outside the sole grant journal.
blockers.finding: permission-truth-tables.v6 fixes ONE durable append-only journal per (project, grant generation), says there is no second ordering authority anywhere in the design, derives order from durable journal sequence rather than arrival, and makes journal durability the gate. v9 instead writes pendingTerminalizerRecord outside that journal, names the FIRST terminalizer that arrived, and lets its presence decide that the terminal marker is the only lawful next append. That external byte therefore orders terminalizers relative to future grant-journal appends and gates the carrier before any terminal marker is durable. The same sole writer does not cure the two-order problem. ID-DEP-P5 lets DR-124 assign class/owner/custody; it does not delegate replacement of the linearization, and SUP-124 names no such displacement.
blockers.requiredRepair: Keep the carrier's order in one durable authority. For example, reserve/preallocate enough journal capacity for the terminal transition and define FIRST by the first durable journal record, or explicitly route a separately named, owner-concurred supersession of the one-order rule with complete atomicity and recovery semantics. Merely calling an external current record SC-OPS or giving it the same writer is insufficient. Do not apply a supersession or mint D-096 (A) in this candidate.

blockers.title: A failed pending-record write can disappear across crash and reopen a carrier after an already-arrived terminalizer.
blockers.finding: The subject expressly handles pendingTerminalizerRecord write failure by keeping capacityPause and forbidding ordinary appends, but that rule has no durable representation when the very write fails. Counterexample: the intact journal reaches a capacity boundary; projectPurge arrives; the external pending write fails; the process crashes; capacity is available at restart. Recovery finds no pending record, and capacityPause's explicit absent branch resumes ordinary appends. The prior projectPurge is lost, so the carrier reopens despite FIRST-wins terminalization. No acknowledgment or refusal rule says the event was unaccepted, and a later different terminalizer could incorrectly become the recorded FIRST.
blockers.requiredRepair: Define a crash-stable admission protocol. A terminalizer must either become durably ordered before it is accepted/acknowledged, or fail with an explicit retryable refusal and be excluded from the FIRST-wins set. Recovery must never use an absent pending record as permission to resume when a previously accepted terminalizer may have failed to persist. Add crash-boundary tests before pending durability, after pending durability/before marker, and after marker/before consumption. The repair must also satisfy SCC-V9-B1's sole-order requirement.

shouldFix.title: The two new external SC-OPS records do not close their inherited journaled/redacted/bounded treatment.
shouldFix.finding: The records have useful owner, backup, purge, migration, and recovery clauses, but their class-rule treatment is incomplete. carrierQuarantineRecord is permanent, cannot be purged normally, and is not dropped to make room; pendingTerminalizerRecord can remain unconsumed when quarantine wins. Neither says how create/consume/clear is journaled or states a finite namespace/lifecycle bound. SUP-124's class-rule displacement is explicitly limited to grant-journal bytes, while both records are explicitly external to the grant journal.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: State the journaled representation and enforceable bound for both external records, including the pending-plus-quarantine composition and consumption audit. If either intentionally needs an unbounded/no-drop exception, add that exact byte set to a named proposed supersession with its owner, reversibility, and D-096 (A) gate; do not silently inherit the grant-journal-only exception.

verdictRule: ACCEPT only when blockers=0 and shouldFix=0.
coordinatorSummary: REJECT at 2 blockers and 1 SHOULD-FIX. v9 places the missing quarantine fact and cleanly splits transient capacity from uncertain-tail loss, but pendingTerminalizerRecord creates an external order contrary to the one-journal contract and its own failed-write path is not crash-stable. The new external SC-OPS records also need explicit treatment under the journaled/redacted/bounded class rule. DR-124 remains OPEN; SUP-124 is not applied; no D-096 (A) grant is minted; implementation remains unauthorized.
